https://www.cei.int/ansa/178237.text: Latvia will build a rocket manufacturing plant (ANSA) - VILNIUS, JUL 25 - The U.S. company Native Trading has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Latvian Ministry of Defense to develop an artillery rocket production facility in Latvia. The complex, whose construction costs range from 70 to 90 million euros, will be responsible not only for building the rockets, but also for producing the solid propellants needed to power them, loading the warheads, performing final assembly, and conducting functional tests. Latvian Defense Minister Viktors Valainis emphasized that the memorandum aims to strengthen the Baltic country's defense capabilities while promoting its economic growth and innovation. (ANSA). https://nineoclock.ro/von-der-leyen-roma.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Ursula von der Leyen: Romania’s Destruction of Explosive-Laden Drone Near Neptun Deep Is “Hybrid Warfare” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Thursday that Romania’s destruction of a naval drone carrying explosives near the Neptun Deep platform in the Black Sea is part of an escalating campaign of threats against the European Union. Romanian authorities said two F-16 aircraft were scrambled after a maritime drone was spotted approximately 80 nautical miles east of Constanța, near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project. One of the aircraft fired its onboard cannon and hit the drone. An EOD team subsequently neutralized it, with authorities confirming that the drone was carrying an explosive charge. In a post published on X, von der Leyen wrote: Today, Romania destroyed a naval drone carrying explosives near its Neptun Deep platform in the Black Sea. An escalating campaign of threats is underway, unsettling our citizens and seeking to divide our Union. This is hybrid warfare. The founding mission of our Union is to preserve peace. Today, that also means having the capacity to deter provocation and aggression. Our Readiness 2030 agenda is mobilising up to EUR 800 billion. With the European Drone Defence Initiative and the Eastern Flank Watch, we are scaling up production in Europe to deliver capabilities Member States need. So we can respond to emerging threats with speed, unity and resolve. Von der Leyen did not directly identify the origin of the drone in her statement. Romanian President Nicușor Dan, however, condemned what he described as an intensification of “irresponsible” incidents by Russia. The incident comes amid growing security concerns surrounding the Black Sea and critical energy infrastructure,particularly the strategically important Neptun Deep gas project. (is associated with: «Lithuania's Nausėda: Drone downed by NATO jets probably Russian») Kay Nietfeld/dpa The drone downed by NATO combat jets over Lithuania is thought to have been a Russian projectile that went off course, President Gitanas Nausėda said after a meeting of the National Security Council in Vilnius on Wednesday. "Based on what we know at present, it was probably a Gerbera-type drone," Nausėda said. He added that it had likely been targeted at Ukraine but was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare and entered Lithuanian airspace. Nausėda said it was likely not a deliberate attack on Lithuania. According to Lithuanian authorities, the drone was equipped with an explosive device and had likely entered Lithuania from neighbouring Belarus. There were no injuries or damage. Authorities had previously warned residents in several regions about a possible aerial threat. There have already been several drone incidents in the Baltic states, which are all EU and NATO members, since the start of the war in Ukraine. Drones intercepted using electronic countermeasures also pose a risk to neighbouring countries. During Ukrainian attacks, off-course drones have repeatedly entered the airspace of the Baltic states, with some subsequently crashing. In the past, Russian-made drones have also flown into Lithuania from Belarus. Nausėda pointed out the risk of further drone incidents and said that the ability to detect drones needed to be improved. Photograph: Justin Sullivan/Getty Images California Southern California prepares for flooding amid forecast of ‘record-breaking tides’ Residents of coastal communities told to avoid beaches during high tides and keep further away from the ocean than usual Dani Anguiano Mon 26 Oct 2026 13.47 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 13.49 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Southern California coastal communities are preparing for days of flooding amid potentially “record-breaking tides” this week. The National Weather Service warned that significant coastal flooding is expected in San Diego and Orange counties through Thursday that could close roads and inundate homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. To the north, a wide swath of the coast from San Luis Obispo county to Los Angeles county could see “minor to moderate” coastal flooding with tides as high as 8ft. “Avoid the beaches during high tides, keep farther back from the ocean than usual (waves will run much farther up the beach that expected), stay off rock walls/jetties, and make sure flood-prone property is protected this week,” the NWS office in San Diego said in a statement. More than a week before the exceptionally high tides were forecast to arrive, the Orange county city of Newport Beach declared a local emergency to prepare for flooding. Staff were deploying across the area to inspect infrastructure, reinforce beach berms and install sandbags and other equipment, the city said. Newport Beach is providing free sandbags and advised residents to inspect vulnerable areas around their properties. Due to El Niño and the Kelvin wave , ocean water levels in the region have already been about 15 to 22in higher than expected, Newport Beach city manager Seimone Jurjis said in a statement . “A foot and a half may not sound like much, but in a coastal community like ours, it can mean the difference between water staying below a seawall and water spilling into streets, garages and homes, especially during some of the highest tides of the year,” Jurjis said. This month has already brought extreme weather in the region, including flooding that overtook city streets and large waves that struck beachside homes. The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel left a trail of destruction in California, significantly damaging homes, destroying a boardwalk and forcing residents to evacuate. With a historic El Niño unfolding in the Pacific, California is expected to face severe storms this winter. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/p.text: Prim-ministrul leton Andris Kulbergs a cerut vineri Europei să adopte o poziţie mai fermă faţă de Rusia şi a afirmat că continentul trebuie să dea dovadă de mai mult curaj ţinând cont că are o putere militară şi o capacitate economică mai mari decât ale Moscovei, informează EFE. „Uitaţi-vă unde este Rusia, nici măcar nu este capabilă să înfrângă o ţară mult mai mică, atât ca teritoriu, cât şi ca populaţie, cum este Ucraina”, a declarat premierul Letoniei la summitul şefilor de stat şi de guvern ai UE, care are loc la Dublin. Kulbergs a asigurat că Ucraina demonstrează „un spirit enorm de rezistenţă” continuând să „facă faţă Rusiei pentru al cincilea an consecutiv”. „Astăzi, tema importantă - a spus el - este inteligenţa artificială, dar există multe alte chestiuni mult mai importante, precum pacea în Ucraina şi dezbaterile despre rolul Europei în negocieri. Cred că Europa trebuie să fie mai curajoasă, pentru că suntem mai mari ca dimensiune, avem o putere militară mai mare şi suntem superiori în toate aspecte economice”. Şeful executivului leton a regretat de asemenea că Moscova poate „să impună cerinţe pe care Europa să fie nevoită să le accepte”, după ce a amintit că Rusia „este ţara agresoare” şi că, în opinia sa, „pierde teren pe front”. „Noi suntem cei care ar trebui să ne creştem exigenţele şi să clarificăm ce garanţii de securitate ar trebui să primească Ucraina”, a adăugat Kulbergs. Uniunea Europeană speră să decidă în următoarele două săptămâni cine o va reprezenta în viitoarele negocieri de pace dintre Ucraina şi Rusia, după ce Statele Unite au invitat europenii să participe direct la contacte. Chestiunea a devenit o prioritate în cadrul întâlnirii informale de vineri, deşi nu era iniţial inclusă pe agendă. Principalii lideri europeni şi-au exprimat dorinţa de a participa la discuţii pentru a apăra interesele Europei şi a sprijini Ucraina, chiar dacă există dezacorduri cu privire la cine ar trebui să preia această reprezentare. De ce nu o vor rușii pe Kaja Kallas la masa negocierilor de pace privind Ucraina.
